key_insight: QPipe uses an LLM-driven multi-agent workflow to turn natural-language requirements into executable quantum applications for test optimization.
engineering_relevance: The approach lowers the quantum/programming expertise barrier for software engineering teams that want to prototype quantum-assisted optimization workflows from real benchmark problems.
method: Specialized agents handle requirement parsing, formulation, code generation, review, execution, and verification.
The system converts each natural-language requirement into a traceable quantum-application workflow.
Ablation studies test the roles of code generation, task knowledge, review feedback, and multi-agent decomposition.
evidence_signal: Across 20 natural-language requirements, QPipe achieved 100% code compilation and 96.7% application execution/final-result combination, with generated solutions often outperforming an offline genetic algorithm baseline.
watch_item: The reported gains depend on substantial LLM token use and successful execution is not guaranteed for every requirement, so deployment may still need human oversight and error handling.
paper_title: Leveraging LLM-Based Agentic Systems to Generate Quantum Applications for Test Optimization
